notes.decision: Reading ⲕⲉ̄ (with overline) as abbreviation of ⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ ('chapter') yielding 'the kephalaion of the Anointed.' Alternative readings: ⲕⲉ as 'another' (giving 'another (chapter of) the Anointed') or ⲕⲉ̄ as Greek κύριε/κύριος ('Lord Christ'). The chapter-content is about Mani-as-Christ being summoned by Sapores; the self-referential 'kephalaion of the Anointed' fits the title-formula. Final ⲭⲉ ⲛ̄ ⲟⲋ̄ functions as 'namely no. 76,' a chapter-number coda.

Translating as triple-titled single referent (Mani): 'our Lord, the Anointed, our Illuminator of Light.' The conjunction ⲙⲛ̄ here links titles rather than coordinating two persons (the singular verb ⲛⲉϩⲍⲙⲉⲥⲧ ⲡⲉ confirms a single subject). In Manichaean Christology Mani identifies as Christ-Paraclete; multi-titled stacking is standard.

Reading as Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲙⲟⲓ̈ 'O that, would that' (wish-particle), with regular Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ. Aurades' wish-introducer fits the petitionary content (request for two more Christ-like figures). Alternative reading as ϩⲁⲙⲏⲛ 'amen/truly' is possible but less idiomatic in this petitionary context.

Translating literally as 'two anointed-ones' (preserving the ⲙⲛⲭⲥ glossary translation 'the Anointed'). Aurades requests two more figures who are 'similar to' Mani — likely a request for additional Christ-like apostolic companions. The repetition ⲙⲛⲭⲥ ⲙⲛⲭⲥ in line 31 emphasizes this petition.

Tentative reading as 'established (of) heart' — possibly Lyc. compound ⲍⲏⲡ-ⲕⲏⲧ where ⲕⲏⲧ derives from ⲕⲱⲧ 'build, establish.' Functions as a moral qualifier in series with ⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲥ 'good' and ⲛⲁⲏⲧ 'merciful' (line 30). Alternative: 'gentle of heart' or 'humble of heart.' Confidence low.

Reading ⲛⲁⲟⲱ as future of ⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'add, dwell' (in glossary; cf. ⲟⲩⲏⲍ 'be set, dwell'); ⲍⲁⲧⲏⲛ = ϩⲁ-ⲧⲏⲛ 'with us / before us' (1pl). Translation 'who shall abide with us in your manner' fits the disciple's request for permanent companion-figures. Alternative ⲛⲁ-ⲁⲱ 'shall multiply/abound' less likely given context.
Translated 'When' as Lycopolitan reflex of the temporal/relative perfect ⲛⲧⲁⲣⲉ-/ⲛⲧⲉⲣⲉ-. The ⲡⲉ is the article on ⲡⲛⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ. Standard Kephalaia narrative-frame opening for a saint's response.
Read as Lycopolitan 'he said to him' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲭⲉϩ 'he said to him'). The ϩ is 3sg.m suffix on indirect object construction; the following ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to him' reinforces this.

Translated as 'declare/make known' throughout this page (lines 4, 9, 13, 20). The verb recurs in contexts of speech-proclamation paralleling ⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ. Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲡ 'reckon, tell, declare.'

Translated 'they did not allow me' / 'they did not give place to me' per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲧϯⲙⲁ 'consign / give over.' The construction parallels line 18 ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲧⲟⲩⲱϣ ⲛⲏⲓ̈ 'they did not permit me.'
Translated 'that I might bring (it) widely.' ⲃⲛ̄ as Lyc. reflex of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring' (cf. line 25 ⲁⲓ̈ⲃⲛ); ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ̄ as adverbial 'widely, broadly' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide').
Translated 'fully' from root ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' (qualitative sense). Modifies ⲉⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ — the mystery is 'fully proclaimed in the living truth.' Could alternatively be reflexive 'in itself.'
Translated 'extension/length' from root ⲁⲓⲉⲩⲧⲉ 'become long, extend' (per accumulated vocab). The phrase ϩⲛ ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ = 'in extension/at length' — the manner of spreading the truth.

Translated 'has constrained me.' ⲗⲱϫϩ as qualitative form (cf. accumulated ⲗⲱⲭⲍ̄ 'defile' but here in transferred sense 'press, constrain') with object ⲙⲙⲁⲓ̈ 'me.' Fits Mani's lament that the world has restricted his open proclamation.

Form ⲁϫⲱ left untranslated as 'saying' tentatively. Could be partial of a longer word, or noun related to ⲱϣ 'cry/proclaim.' The collocation ⲁϫⲱ ϩⲛ ⲛⲉϩⲁⲟⲣⲙⲁ 'speaking/saying in his visions' fits the parable-discourse context of Mani.
Greek καί ταῦτα 'and these things,' transliterated. Functions as discourse-connective 'moreover, and these things being so.'

Translated 'heed/yield to.' Per accumulated vocab on ⲍⲩⲡⲟⲁⲉϫⲉ ('counselor' as 'one who speaks under'), the verbal here is Greek ὑπο- + Coptic ⲥⲉϫⲉ 'speak' = 'submit-by-speech, hearken.' In negation: 'they did not heed me.'

Left as 'ⲣⲁⲛ' untranslated at start of line 22. Possibly the tail of a word from line 21 ('the name,' ⲡⲣⲁⲛ; or 'to us,' end of [ⲁⲣⲁ]ⲛ; or 'again,' particle ⲁⲛ). Without secure parallels, transliteration is preserved.

Translated 'I bore necessity.' ⲃⲛ̄ as Lyc. perfect of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ/ϥⲓ 'carry, bear' (parallel to line 8 ⲛⲧⲁⲃⲛ̄ 'that I bring'). The ⲁⲛⲁⲅⲕⲏ (Greek ἀνάγκη 'compulsion, distress') paired with sea-voyage imagery suggests perilous straits.

Form left untranslated. Possible parsings: ϫⲉ-ⲩ-ⲁⲃⲓ 'that they thirst' (cf. ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲃⲉ in glossary), ϫⲉ-ⲩ-ⲁⲃⲓ 'that they be sanctified' (ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ qualitative), or ϫⲉ-ⲉⲩ-ⲁⲃⲓ 'that they be coming.' Without context, marked as uncertain.
Form ⲁⲩⲟⲩⲱ left as fragment 'they ⲟⲩⲱ.' Could be 'they finished/already' (auxiliary ⲟⲩⲱ 'have done'), or partial of a longer verb broken at line edge.
Form left as transliterated fragment. Possibly Lyc. ⲱϫⲛ̄ 'fail, perish' (cf. accumulated ⲱⲝⲛⲉ 'cease/fail') yielding 'they failed/became weary.' Alternatively from ϫⲱⲛϥ̄ 'rise up.' Tentative.

Translated 'a single Anointed' (recurring lines 3, 6, 17). The ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ emphasizes Mani's claim to be the one and unique apostolic figure of his time — paralleling apostolic uniqueness traditions. Per glossary entry ⲡⲙⲛ̄ⲭⲥ → 'the Anointed.'

Translated 'I ceased while (being/speaking)...' Lycopolitan ⲗⲟ + circumstantial = standard 'cease, leave off.' The contextual sense is puzzling: Mani says he 'ceased while in light' and 'ceased while speaking with frankness,' which seems to contradict his subsequent assertion of bold proclamation. Possibilities: (a) Mani is reporting that his frank speech was silenced under pressure but he persevered; (b) ⲗⲟ here functions inceptively in this dialect ('I came to be' rather than 'I left off'); (c) the underlying form is ⲁⲗⲉ 'rise up' (ⲁⲓ̈ⲗⲟ ← ⲁⲓ̈ⲁⲗⲟ in Lycopolitan reduction). I retain the standard 'cease' rendering as the most defensible literal reading.

Translated 'before me' following the example given in the system prompt. Literally 'against me / toward me' (preposition ⲟⲩⲃⲉ + 1sg suffix), but in this idiom with ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ the locative sense 'in my presence, before me' is intended.

Translated 'their innermost.' Lycopolitan ⲍⲛⲧ = ϩⲏⲧ 'belly, interior, midst' with 3pl possessive ⲟⲩ 'their.' Distinct from ⲡⲍⲏⲧ 'heart' (also a possible reading). Cf. line 24 ⲍⲛ ⲧⲟⲩⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'in their midst' as a parallel.

Translated tentatively 'under one [house?].' ⲟⲩⲏⲓ̈ in Lycopolitan can mean 'house/family' (Sahidic ⲏⲓ̈) or possibly 'one' (numeral). Given the parallel of officials gathered in council, 'under one [roof/house]' fits, but the reading is uncertain.

Translated 'counselors.' This appears to be a Greek-Coptic hybrid: Greek prefix ὑπο- 'under, secretly' + Lycopolitan ⲥⲉϫⲉ 'speak' (note ⲥ→ⲁ here is unusual; possibly a scribal feature or different etymology). The compound denotes those who speak in private counsel — court advisors. The same compound recurs in line 11 governing 'me,' confirming the agent/verbal sense ('they counsel me' / 'counselors').
Greek loanword μεγιστᾶνες 'magnates, grandees' — the high nobility of the Sasanian court. Translated 'magnates' to preserve the rank-specific sense.
Greek loanword συγκλητικοί 'members of the council, senators.' Translated 'senators.' Forms a triad with magnates (line 5) and satraps + governors (line 6) describing the Sasanian royal court.
Greek ἡγεμών 'leader, governor.' Translated 'governors.' In Sasanian context, regional administrators alongside satraps.
'Was long-suffering' per accumulated vocabulary; Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲣⲟϣ 'be heavy, slow.' The pair ⲍⲣⲁⲱ + ⲍⲣⲁⲙ (line 10) maintains the twin discipline of patient endurance and silence.
Tentatively rendered 'command(?).' May be ⲟⲩⲉϩⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command, decree' shortened, or ⲟⲩⲏϩ qualitative 'be set, dwell.' In court context the 'royal command' reading suits, but uncertain.
Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- 'one who does' + ⲣ̄- 'do' + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' = 'sinners' (doers of sin). Direct reflection of the Coptic morphology.

Translated 'drawing me into.' ϩⲧⲱⲕ likely Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲱⲧⲕ̄ 'draw, pull' (Crum 720b). With ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward, into,' it describes the counselors' attempt to pull Mani into some position or compromise.

Tentatively rendered 'embrace(?).' The form is partially restored ([ⲍⲱ]ⲙϩ); etymology uncertain. Possible roots: (a) ⲱⲙϩ as variant of an embracing/holding verb; (b) a noun for image/manifestation. The contrast 'world loves darkness, hates the X of light' suggests X is a positive aspect/contact with light. 'Embrace' captures this active sense without overcommitting to a specific form-vocabulary term (which would conflict with ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ/ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ usage).
Translated 'I crossed.' From ϫⲱⲣ 'spread, cross, traverse,' specifically of crossing seas. The s-causative or qualitative form ⲝⲟⲟⲣⲉ is the standard verb for crossing water in Coptic.

Tentatively rendered 'crossed.' The form is unusual; possibly a reduplicated stem related to ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' or to ⲡⲱⲧ 'flee/run,' or a special verb for sea-crossing. Context (sea-crossing narrative) supports 'cross' translation.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲧⲁϣⲉⲟⲉⲓϣ 'proclaim, preach.' Standard Manichaean missionary verb; Mani proclaiming the truth before authorities.

Translated 'while I dwell.' Word split across lines 23/24: ⲉⲓ̈ⲍ on line 23 + [ⲙ]ⲁⲥ on line 24. Lycopolitan ⲍⲙⲁⲥⲧ = Sahidic ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ qualitative 'sit, dwell, remain,' with circumstantial prefix ⲉⲓ̈- 'while I (am).'
'The power of the Father.' ⲧⲃⲁⲙ = ⲧϭⲟⲙ 'the power' (Lycopolitan ⲃ for ϭ). ⲡⲓⲱⲧ = the Father (of Greatness in Manichaean usage). Despite damage, this phrase is recoverable with high confidence.

Parsed as exclamative '(with) power, how greatly they bear (a labor)' based on parallel with line 20 ⲥⲉⲃⲓ ⲍⲁ ⲛ̄ⲡⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'they bear under the kings.' ⲟⲛⲟⲁⲙ may be variant of ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'power' with prosthetic vowel, or ⲟⲩⲛ̄-ⲟⲁⲙ 'there is power.' ϩⲃⲓ is the verb ⲃⲓ 'bear, carry' with relative/circumstantial ϩ-prefix.

Translated tentatively as 'his command/decree.' The lexeme is unclear; possible analyses include: (a) ⲡⲉϥ-ⲟⲩⲉϩⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'his command' (abbreviated); (b) ⲡⲉϥ-ⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'his joining/agreement'; (c) ⲡⲉϥ-ⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ 'his decree.' Imperial-administrative context (king moving his ⲟⲱⲧⲏ̄ among satraps) supports a decree/command sense.

Translated as 'he received upon him' = 'he took to himself.' ⲁⲭⲓ likely Lyc. for ⲁϥϫⲓ (3sg.m perfect of ϫⲓ 'take, receive'); ⲁⲣⲁϩ = 'upon/to him.' Subject is the singular king (cf. ⲡⲉϩⲟⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲙ 'his power') from previous lines.
Translated tentatively as 'behold!' (imperative ⲁⲛⲁⲩ) or 'they shall see' (future). Could also be misreading. Sense uncertain.

Translated as 'they bear' from ⲃⲓ 'carry, endure (a burden).' Direct parallel with line 1 ϩⲃⲓ. The construction describes the populace's subjection to imperial authority — the people 'bear under the kings' (i.e., are subjects of the Persian/Sasanian crown) and 'receive' the orders of caesars, satraps, and governors.
Translated 'caesars' (Greek καῖσαρ) — generic term for emperor, here likely referring to imperial authorities of either Sasanian or Roman jurisdictions encountered in Mani's mission.

Translated 'Maïzanos' = the city/region of Mesene (Maishan), the Sasanian province at the head of the Persian Gulf where Mani is reported to have established an early mission. Standard transliteration.
Translated 'the land of Babylon, the city of the Assyrians' = Sasanian Asuristan (Babylonia / Mesopotamia), the heartland province where Ctesiphon lay. Standard Manichaean missionary geography.

ⲡⲣⲁⲓ̈ rendered 'kings' (Lyc plural, in accumulated vocabulary); ⲛⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ rendered 'wellsprings' per accumulated tentative gloss (ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ 'wellspring/source'). The pair functions as a fixed doublet on this page (recurring lines 6, 11, 23-24) for political-spiritual elites of a region.

ⲉⲛⲉ here read as the irrealis-conditional particle 'were it not / if not,' setting up the counterfactual continuing through lines 7-10: 'were it not for the Father's strength, they would not have left me one day in Babylon.' Fits the autobiographical apologia structure.

Translated 'for service under the kings.' ⲉϩⲃ̅ taken as ⲉ- + ϩⲃⲁ 'service, work-state,' rendering the imperial-administrative carrying-capacity image. Alternative readings include 'in subjection under' (ϩⲃⲁ as 'subjection') or '(power) of work under.' All preserve the sense that the Assyrian land sustains the imperial structure.

Rendered 'it has not been turned (aside)' — ⲅⲱⲧⲡ̅ taken as Lyc reflex of a verb of overturning/turning aside (cf. ⲕⲱⲧⲡ̄/ϭⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'turn aside,' or related to ϫⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'gather, be set upon'). Paired with preceding ⲡⲓϥⲕⲓⲙ 'it did not move' as a doublet for the kingdom's immovability before its enemies.

Rendered 'this laying-bare of heart' to preserve the literal sense of ⲕⲱⲕ (in glossary ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ 'strip naked'); ⲕⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ literally 'stripping/laying-bare of heart' = openness, candidness. Distinct from but semantically related to ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' in glossary; possibly a Lyc variant. The image fits Mani's testimony that the Medes/Parthians responded with sincere disclosure.

Read as negative perfect 3sg.m: 'But he himself did not find likewise to receive him.' Subject-referent ambiguous; likely the cosmic Adversary (Errant/Sin) who was unable to seize Mani because the power of truth moved everything. Alternative: 'his (Mani's) finding likewise to receive him,' a participial reading. Negative reading taken as default given parallelism with positive ⲁϩⲅⲛⲅⲙ̅ 'they found' in line 23.

ⲛⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ here functions as 'the manner / the form,' likely Lyc variant or related to ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness.' With ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'whole' and ⲙⲡⲥⲙⲁⲧ 'of the form,' the phrase suggests universal correspondential transformation. Translated 'at the entire manner of the form.'

Coptic preserved as transcribed; treated as scribal abbreviation/typo for ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ 'the Apostle.' Translated 'the Apostle' since the discourse-formula 'Then said the Apostle to the disciple' is the standard Kephalaia frame.

Rendered 'I am one Anointed' — ⲡⲙⲛ̄ⲭⲥ per glossary = 'the Anointed/the Christ.' Translation 'one Anointed' preserves the unity-uniqueness emphasis (Mani as unique apostolic Christ-figure, not 'a Christ among others'). With ⲛⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'single, sole.'

Rendered 'wickedness' tentatively. Etymology unclear: possibly Lyc abstract on ⲃⲱⲱⲛ 'wicked' (with phonological shift) or related to ⲃⲏϫⲉ/ⲃⲏⲍⲉ 'lack/deficiency.' Context (paired with ⲇⲁⲙⲁⲍⲉ 'subdue' applied to dark powers) supports a moral-defective sense. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Translated 'a host of multitude' tentatively. ⲧⲱⲣ may be Lyc for ⲧⲱⲱⲣⲉ 'hand' (= 'a handful/quantity of multitude') or possibly an idiom for 'a great number.' Sense secured by parallel context with line 4 'two Anointed.'

Read as ⲙ̄-ⲡⲁ-ⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'from my midst forth.' Mani's rhetorical question contemplates whether two Christs could come 'from his midst' — i.e., whether his single Christological identity could be doubled. Could alternatively be a compound preposition.

Read as ⲛⲁ- (future) + ϣⲱⲡ 'receive, hold' in Lyc reduced spelling, giving 'shall hold/contain (under them).' The cosmic-spatial sense (what place could contain two Christs?) fits the rhetorical context of lines 4-6.
Greek loan ὑποδέχομαι 'receive, accept.' Lyc orthography ⲍ for ὑ-onset and ⲁⲉ for δε. Modal ϣ- 'be able' restored: 'is able to receive them.'

Mani's self-identification as 'one Anointed' marks the section break following the disciple's question about multiple Christs. The mid-line leer signals the structural transition from question to answer.

Likely Lyc plural ⲛ̄ⲣ̄ⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'the temples (of heaven)' = celestial sanctuaries. Cf. accumulated vocab ⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ. Mani's claim: 'I walk in the heart of the heavenly temples,' affirming his pancosmic presence as the single Anointed.

Translated 'outwardly' as ϣⲁ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'until/unto-the-outside' = external manifestation. The Anointed who exists internally in the disciples shall be made manifest outwardly. Could alternatively be ϣⲱ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'remain forth.' Sense is the manifestation of the indwelling Christ.

Read as ⲛⲉⲓ̈ⲉⲧ ('I declare') + -ⲧⲏⲛⲉ ('you, pl.') giving 'whom I declare' or 'I am declaring to you.' Per accumulated vocabulary entry. The construction with preceding ⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲧⲛⲉ 'you' is rhetorical apposition: 'But you, you whom I declare...'
ⲙⲁⲍⲕ = ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ-ⲕ 'grasp you'; ⲛⲁϣ- modal 'be able.' Translated 'who shall be able to grasp you' = who has power to repay the apostle. Standard Coptic recompense-verb usage.
Greek loanword ἱκανός 'sufficient, able.' Lyc ⲍ for spiritus before ⲓ. Functions substantivally: 'the able one' = the only one capable of recompensing.
